A.name: Normal running
A.what: All machines run normally for a few minutes.

B.name: Lone spike
B.what: One reading is far too high, then readings go back to normal.

C.name: Sustained warning
C.what: Motor 1 temperature stays above its warning limit for more than 10 seconds.

D.name: Sustained critical
D.what: A reading stays above its critical limit for more than 10 seconds.

E.name: Two faults at once
E.what: Motor 2 temperature and current both go abnormal together.

G.name: Bad reading
G.what: A reading arrives as text, or empty, or impossible (for example 9999 degrees).

H.name: Connection cut
H.what: The link between the parts is cut for a while, then restored.

J.name: Storage fails
J.what: The main store becomes unavailable or full.

K.name: Restart
K.what: The system is stopped and started again.

L.name: Maintenance
L.what: An Engineer puts a machine into maintenance for a short time and lets it run past the time.

M.name: Fault returns
M.what: A fault stays open, then clears, then comes back.

N.name: Limit change
N.what: An Engineer changes limits, including one that is not allowed.

O.name: Nobody connected
O.what: A fault happens while no Operator or Engineer is signed in.

P.name: Noisy readings
P.what: Readings are full of noise and some are damaged.

Q.name: Heavy load
Q.what: 10 machines and 5 users at the same time.

R.name: Slow alert
R.what: An alert is made to arrive more than 2 seconds late.

S.name: Labelled test set
S.what: A set of readings where the right answer is known, to count how many faults are found.

T.name: Login checks
T.what: Wrong passwords, short passwords, common passwords and a user without permission.

U.name: Near and remote mode
U.what: Switch between the near-range and remote-range modes.

V.name: Old data
V.what: Readings older than 24 hours, some from normal windows and some from fault windows.

FR-1.steps: Open the Overview and look at a motor card.
FR-1.pass: Temperature, current, vibration and RPM are all shown.

FR-2.steps: Open the Overview and look at a water pump card.
FR-2.pass: Bearing temperature, current, vibration and RPM are all shown.

FR-3.steps: Open the Overview and look at a backup power card.
FR-3.pass: Internal temperature, current and fan speed are all shown.

FR-3a.steps: Count the readings for one parameter over one minute.
FR-3a.pass: About 60 readings, one each second, for every parameter.

FR-4.steps: Play the scenario and watch Motor 1.
FR-4.pass: The high temperature is flagged for Motor 1.

FR-5.pass: The status shows warning, then critical, naming the machine and parameter.

FR-6.pass: No fault is raised from one reading. A fault only appears when it lasts across the 10-second check.

FR-7.steps: Play the scenario with an Operator and an Engineer signed in, one near and one remote.
FR-7.pass: A pop-up appears on both screens.

FR-7a.pass: It shows the machine, parameter, fault type, level and time.

FR-7b.steps: Sign in as the Administrator while the scenario plays.
FR-7b.pass: No pop-up and no fault bell list.

FR-7c.steps: Play the scenario with nobody signed in, then sign in as an Operator.
FR-7c.pass: The fault is still open and its pop-up appears.

FR-8.pass: The pop-up goes away for that person.

FR-8a.steps: After acknowledging, open the machine's fault list.
FR-8a.pass: It shows who acknowledged and when.

FR-8b.steps: After acknowledging, look at the fault again.
FR-8b.pass: It is still open, not resolved.

FR-9.steps: Open the machine's history and graph.
FR-9.pass: The fault and the readings can be called up.

FR-9a.steps: Look at the stored statuses in the database.
FR-9a.pass: One status with a time for every 10 seconds.

FR-9b.steps: Load the old data and look at what is kept.
FR-9b.pass: Readings of old normal windows are gone. Readings of old warning or critical windows are still there with their status.

FR-10.steps: Sign in as each role and open fault history. As an Operator or Engineer, generate a report.
FR-10.pass: Everyone can view history. Operator and Engineer can make a report showing performance and repeated faults.

FR-11.steps: Switch the demo between near and remote mode.
FR-11.pass: The dashboard shows the same equipment data in both modes.

FR-12.steps: Cut the connection, wait, then restore it.
FR-12.pass: The dashboard keeps showing local data. After restoring, the stored readings arrive.

FR-13.pass: Within 3 seconds it shows a sensor fault, not the last number.

FR-14.steps: Send the three kinds of bad reading.
FR-14.pass: Each one is kept out, logged as invalid, and the system carries on.

FR-15.pass: Two separate fault records appear, one for each parameter.

FR-16.steps: Let a fault stay open, then clear, then return.
FR-16.pass: No second alert while it is open. A new alert only after it cleared and came back.

FR-17.steps: As an Engineer, mark the acknowledged fault resolved. Try as an Operator.
FR-17.pass: The Engineer can, and the time is recorded. The Operator cannot.

FR-18.steps: As an Engineer, turn on maintenance for a stated time.
FR-18.pass: Readings keep recording. New fault alerts for that machine pause.

FR-19.steps: Let the stated time run out.
FR-19.pass: The machine shows an overdue mark.

FR-20.pass: New readings are kept in temporary storage, the system keeps running, and the event is logged.

FR-21.pass: It carries on with the last settings, and machines show their status again once new readings arrive.

FR-21a.pass: An alert goes to the Administrator only.

FR-22.steps: Add a user, register a machine and change a limit, then open the change log.
FR-22.pass: Each change is listed with who and when.

FR-23.steps: Change a limit, then look at its earlier values.
FR-23.pass: The old value and the date of change are still shown.

FR-23a.steps: As an Engineer, change a warning and a critical limit in Settings.

FR-23b.steps: Try a warning limit that is not below the critical limit.

FR-23c.steps: Change a limit, then send readings between the old and new limit.
FR-23c.pass: New readings use the new limit. Earlier readings are unchanged.

FR-23d.steps: Raise a fault, change the limit, then open the fault.
FR-23d.pass: The fault shows the limit that was in force when it was raised.

FR-24.steps: Open the Overview and the machines list.
FR-24.pass: Several motors appear as separate units, each with its own status and fault history.

FR-25.steps: Compare the time stamps from different parts of the system for the same reading.

FR-26.steps: Set the sign-out time to 1 minute and leave the screen idle.
FR-26.pass: The person is signed out and must sign in again. 1 minute and 5 minutes are accepted, 6 is not.

FR-27.steps: Sign in as an Operator and try to open the Admin page.

FR-28.steps: Open a page without signing in.

FR-28a.steps: Set a 7-character, an 8-character and a 64-character password.

FR-28b.steps: Set a long password with only lowercase letters.
FR-28b.pass: It is accepted, and nothing forces a change later.

FR-28d.pass: The account is blocked for 15 minutes and the message says so.

FR-28e.steps: Look at the address and the connection details in the browser.
FR-28e.pass: It uses https with TLS 1.2 or newer.

FR-28f.steps: Look at how a password is stored.
FR-28f.pass: It is scrambled and cannot be read back.

NFR-1.steps: Run the labelled set and count critical temperature and current faults found.

NFR-2.steps: Run the labelled set and count vibration faults found.

NFR-5.steps: Read the system's own uptime record for the session.
NFR-5.pass: Data logging was running at least 95% of the time.

NFR-6.steps: Compare readings generated with readings stored, including during the cut.

NFR-7.pass: Valid readings stay valid. Readings that cannot be checked are thrown away, not acted on.

NFR-8.steps: Open the Overview on one laptop screen.
NFR-8.pass: Every machine's status is visible without opening a second window.

NFR-9.steps: Show the code for one parameter's logic, then change it.
NFR-9.pass: Only that part changes. Nothing unrelated needs editing.

NFR-10.steps: Look at stored statuses and warning or critical records as storage grows.
NFR-10.pass: Nothing is deleted automatically before 75% is reached. Normal readings still go after 24 hours.

PR-001.steps: Check the time between status updates for each machine.

PR-001a.steps: Time from the status confirming a critical fault to the alert on screen.

PR-001b.pass: The alert still shows, the delay is logged, and an Alerts delayed notice appears.

PR-002.steps: Time from a reading arriving to it appearing on the dashboard.

PR-003.steps: Run 10 machines at once and watch the update times.
PR-003.pass: Status and reading times stay within their limits.

PR-004.steps: Open the dashboard on 5 screens at once.
PR-004.pass: Status and reading times stay within their limits.

PR-005.steps: Count readings processed each second with 10 machines of 4 parameters.

PR-006.steps: Check the room the store has for readings.
PR-006.pass: Room for at least 3,456,000 readings plus statuses and faults.

PR-007.steps: Time from launch until monitoring is active.
